description.narrative: The proposed program is designed to improve access to finance and the international payment system. The program aims to improve individuals' and businesses' access to financial services, thereby fostering economic growth and livelihood opportunities. The program will strengthen the regulatory and institutional framework governing access to domestic and international financial services that support payments, remittances, credit, and capital, and support households and businesses in creating employment and trade opportunities.

Action 1: To enable the use of digital ID for facilitating increased access to formal financial services: (i) the NEC approved a digital ID policy for nationwide adoption of digital ID services across public and private sectors; and (ii) the DICT completed a digital ID pilot that informed operational, regulatory, and technology requirements for a digital ID policy and implementation roadmap.

Action 3: To assess supply and demand challenges for microfinance, BPNG completed a review of the Current State of Microfinance in PNG.
Action 4: To improve financial inclusion, BPNG: (i) endorsed and declared its intention to implement the We-Fi Code; (ii) undertook a diagnostic assessment of the availability of data on women MSMEs and banks' capability to serve them; and (iii) implemented a We-Fi Code awareness event for finance sector stakeholders (in government and the private sector).
Action 1: To complete the design phase of the Digital ID rollout, DICT will approve and commence implementation of a structured and comprehensive framework to guide execution, alignment with regulatory frameworks, and the advancement of national strategic priorities.
Action 2: To protect the interests of consumers of financial products and services, including vulnerable segments: (i) DOT will submit for NEC approval a Financial Consumer Protection Bill, (ii) BPNG will issue regulations and guidance notes for implementing a new financial consumer protection framework and establish a unit to implement the framework, and (iii) To implement the comprehensive credit reporting requirement endorsed for legal review in Subprogram 1, BPNG will obtain NEC approval for the regulations, issue guidance, and provide training to the industry.
Action 3: To scale up access to microfinance, the government will implement recommendations from the review of the Current State of Microfinance in PNG (undertaken in Subprogram 1).
